instruction: Split the mixed employee data in column A into separate fields (First Name, Last Name, Rank) in columns B, C, and D. After splitting, verify that you have exactly 21 unique job titles.

metadata.explanation: Task requires splitting employee data from column A into columns B (First Name), C (Last Name), D (Rank), and verifying all 21 unique ranks are present. Verified with Python: 21 unique ranks, each appearing exactly once in the gold file.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 30% for column B (first names), 30% for column C (last names), 40% for column D (correct rank counts)

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator now checks ALL three requirements - column B (first names), column C (last names), and column D (ranks with correct counts).
Multi-component scoring properly implemented: 30% weight for first names, 30% for last names, 40% for rank counts - matches the stated scoring breakdown in metadata.
Getter extracts all necessary data: Reads columns B, C, D and returns counts for each, plus split_performed flag.
Metric logic correctly verifies each component: Checks num_first_names == 21, num_last_names == 21, and exact rank counts match expected values.
Partial credit logic is sensible: Awards proportional credit if columns B/C have partial data, and proportional credit for matched ranks.
